title.narrative: Addressing Critical Lean Season WASH Gaps to Support Nutrition and Health Outcomes in Damboa LGA

description.narrative: ltpgtThe lean season in Northeast Nigeria has intensified the nutrition crisis, with 2.6 million children projected to suffer acute malnutrition in 2025, including 1 million at risk of severe acute malnutrition (SAM). In Damboa LGA, where GBVS conducted a WASH–Nutrition Needs Assessment in June 2025, the convergence of unsafe water, inadequate sanitation, and low hygiene coverage is directly worsening nutrition outcomes. The assessment revealed 85 SAM admissions within three months, 80% of caregivers relying on unsafe water, a latrine-to-user ratio of 1:150, and fewer than 30% of households receiving hygiene kits. These gaps heighten diarrhoeal disease transmission, delay SAM recovery, and increase child mortality. Findings were presented and validated at the June 2025 Damboa LCG, confirming GBVS’s operational presence and recognized coordination role (Minutes prepared by UNOCHA and assessment report/Damboa Service Mapping are attached to this proposal).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis 6-month project aims to provide lifesaving WASH services to 9,000 conflict-affected IDPs, returnees host community in Damboa LGA. In line with the NHF SA2 2025 allocation strategy, the intervention will deliver: (i) provision of safe water through trucking, new SMBH rehabilitation of boreholes (ii) rehabilitation, desludging, and construction of gender-segregated, disability-accessible sanitation facilities (iii) targeted distribution of WASH NFIs, prioritizing households with SAM and cholera cases (iv) hygiene promotion campaigns focusing on safe water handling, handwashing, cholera prevention, and menstrual hygiene management (v) cholera rapid response (CATI) to ensure outbreak control within 48–72 hours and (vi) integration of WASH supplies (aquatabs, soap, jerry cans) into the Damboa Stabilization Centre and OTP sites.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtCritical to this project is capacity strengthening of frontline staff and community structures. All Stabilization Centre personnel, support staff, and volunteers will receive training in chlorine monitoring, safe water handling, hygiene promotion, and cholera/SAM case follow-up, replicating successful models from GBVS’s past WASH projects in Damboa. In addition, WASH committees (WASHCOMs) and hygiene promoters will be trained and equipped to ensure local ownership, rapid facility maintenance, and sustained impact.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtImplementation will be led by GBVS, a national NGO with proven experience in Damboa, in partnership with Maple Leaf Early Years Foundation (MLEYF) as sub-grantee, responsible for handpump rehabilitation, community-based hygiene promotion, inclusive mobilization of women, caregivers, and persons with disabilities, CATI logistics, and support for WASHCOM structures. This partnership reinforces NHF’s localization agenda by leveraging national and local capacities for delivery and sustainability.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtCross-cutting principles are central: (i) GBV risk mitigation through gender-segregated, well-lit sanitation facilities and referral linkages (ii) Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) through community inclusion, helpdesks, complaint boxes, and hotlines integrated with WASHCOMs (iii) Gender Equality, ensuring women and adolescent girls are prioritized and participate in decision-making (GAM) and (iv) Disability Inclusion, with ~5% of the budget reserved for accessibility features and engagement of Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention shall cover host communities/returnees. Areas include General Hospital, Haiusari Camp, Wuyaram, Kachalla Burari Kura/Gana, and informal camps. By addressing the WASH–nutrition nexus, the project will reduce preventable deaths, improve recovery outcomes for malnourished children, and enhance the dignity and resilience of 9,000 vulnerable people in Damboa during the lean season. The approach is evidence-based, sector-aligned, and coordinated, ensuring maximum lifesaving impact within six months.ltbrgtlt/pgt
